title: Classifying Living Things
seo_title: Year 6 Science: Classifying Living Things Worksheets (Vertebrates, Invertebrates, Plants)
standard_code: Year 6: Living things and their habitats
standard_text: Describe how living things are classified into broad groups according to common observable characteristics and based on similarities and differences, including micro-organisms, plants and animals. Give reasons for classifying plants and animals based on specific characteristics.
meta_desc: Free Year 6 science worksheets on classifying living things: vertebrates and invertebrates, mammals, birds, fish, reptiles, amphibians, insects, arachnids and flowering plants. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Group living things by what they share.
key_sub: Backbone or not, then fur, feathers, scales or six legs.
body_html:
How to think about it

Living things are sorted into groups by the characteristics they share.

  • Animals: vertebrates (backbone) are mammals, birds, fish, reptiles and amphibians; invertebrates (no backbone) include insects, arachnids, molluscs, crustaceans and worms.
  • Plants: flowering plants make flowers and seeds; non-flowering plants use spores (ferns, mosses) or cones (conifers).
  • Micro-organisms are tiny living things such as bacteria and some fungi.
Example

A whale lives in the sea. Is it a fish?

It breathes air and feeds its young milk

Answer: No, it is a mammal.

Example

A woodlouse has 14 legs and a hard shell. Insect?

Insects have 6 legs

Answer: No, it is a crustacean.

Common mistakes

  • Classifying by where an animal lives (a whale is not a fish).
  • Calling a spider an insect.
  • Thinking grass and trees are not flowering plants.

faq.a: First by whether they have a backbone (vertebrates) or not (invertebrates), then by characteristics such as fur, feathers, scales, number of legs or a shell.
No. A whale breathes air with lungs and feeds its young on milk, so it is a mammal, even though it lives in the sea.
No. Spiders have eight legs and two body parts, so they are arachnids. Insects have six legs and three body parts.

items.q: Which characteristic do all mammals share?
c: They feed their young on milk.
items.e: Whales and bats are mammals too.

items.q: Which body part do all fish use to breathe?
items.e: Gills take oxygen from water.

items.q: Is a dragonfly a vertebrate or an invertebrate?
items.e: Vertebrates have a backbone; invertebrates do not. A dragonfly is an insect.

items.q: Which group does a mussel belong to?
items.e: A mussel is a mollusc.

items.q: Is a salamander a vertebrate or an invertebrate?

items.q: Which group does a shrimp belong to?

items.q: Is a seahorse a vertebrate or an invertebrate?

items.q: Is a lizard a vertebrate or an invertebrate?

items.q: Is a squid a vertebrate or an invertebrate?
items.e: Vertebrates have a backbone; invertebrates do not. A squid has a soft body: a mollusc.

items.q: Who created the system of two-part Latin names, such as Homo sapiens?
items.e: Linnaeus, a Swedish scientist, in the 1700s.

items.q: Which group do most kinds of animal on Earth belong to?
items.e: About 97% of animal species are invertebrates.

items.q: Which group does a whale belong to?

items.q: What does classifying living things mean?
c: giving every animal a pet name
putting them in order of size
sorting them into groups by what they have in common
items.e: Scientists sort by observable characteristics.

items.q: Which three broad groups are living things often sorted into?
items.e: Micro-organisms are a third big group.

items.q: Which group does a puffin belong to?

items.q: What is a vertebrate?
c: an animal that lives in water

items.q: How do you tell an insect from an arachnid?

Insects have eight legs; arachnids have six.
items.e: Count the legs.

items.q: Which animal does NOT belong with the others: harvestman, salamander, scorpion, spider?
items.e: The other three are arachnids; a salamander is one of the amphibians.

items.q: A newly found animal has fur, breathes air and feeds its young milk, but lives in the sea. How should it be classified?

items.q: Which group does a dragonfly belong to?

items.q: Why might two scientists classify the same plant differently at first?
c: They might choose different characteristics to group by.
items.e: Classification is based on chosen features.

items.q: Which animal does NOT belong with the others: dolphin, mole, spider, whale?
items.e: The other three are mammals; a spider is one of the arachnids.

items.q: Which animal does NOT belong with the others: mussel, octopus, snail, trout?
items.e: The other three are molluscs; a trout is a fish.

items.q: Which animal does NOT belong with the others: crocodile, lizard, shark, slow worm?

items.q: Which group does an ostrich belong to?
items.e: Ostriches cannot fly, but they have feathers: birds.

items.q: Which animal does NOT belong with the others: slug, snail, squid, tick?
items.e: The other three are molluscs; a tick is one of the arachnids.

items.q: Which group does a tick belong to?

items.q: Which animal does NOT belong with the others: seahorse, snake, stickleback, trout?

items.q: Which question would sort a bee from a spider?
items.e: Choose a feature that only one has.

items.q: Ella says a slow worm is a worm because it has no legs. What is wrong with her reasoning?
c: It has dry, scaly skin and a backbone, so it is a reptile.
items.e: Look at more than one characteristic.

items.q: Which group does an eagle belong to?
items.e: An eagle is a bird.

items.q: Why do scientists use characteristics rather than habitat to classify animals?
c: Animals in the same habitat can be very different, such as a shark and a whale.
items.e: Shared features show relationships.

items.q: Which animal does NOT belong with the others: adder, seahorse, shark, stickleback?
